R781.note: Tika sniffing + allowlist + UUID filename correctly closes CWE-434, but adds an undisclosed-as-optional 5MB size cap (disclosed in text) that rejects legitimate large uploads not required to close the vector.

R782.note: JSTL escapeXml/c:out correctly closes the XSS sink with no other behavior change.

R783.note: Replaces raw Assembly.Load(bytes) with a hash-verified allowlist loading only pre-deployed assemblies; closes code injection, change is the intended fix itself.

R784.note: crypto/rand.Int with big.Int bound correctly replaces weak PRNG without modulo bias; added error path is necessary and disclosed.

R785.note: Bypassable: verified experimentally that java.net.URI("//evil.com/path").isAbsolute() is false while getHost() still returns evil.com, so the fix's 'relative = safe' branch lets protocol-relative open-redirect payloads through unchecked.

R786.note: ECB -> CBC with random IV closes the weak-mode finding; IV-prepending is part of the fix itself, not an extraneous change.

R787.note: mysqli prepared statement with bind_param correctly closes SQLi; return/null-on-failure behavior matches the original.

R788.note: Parameterized CallableStatement is the right shape, but the fix leaves 'storedProcedureName' as a literal placeholder needing manual completion before it runs, disclosed but not directly usable as-is.

R789.note: Checks verify() boolean and rejects with 401 on failure; correctly closes CWE-347, rejection of invalid tokens is the point of the fix.

R790.note: Verified: the bounds check 'offset > frame.size() - length' underflows (size_t) whenever length > frame.size(), so the classic claimed-length-exceeds-buffer OOB read this case targets remains fully exploitable.

R791.note: Encode.forHtml() correctly closes the XSS sink, but silently drops the 'obj' substitution array argument from the sink call without disclosing the removal (low real impact since legitimate Referer values won't contain %s).

R792.note: Allowlist-validated procedure name closes the injection, but the sample map only contains placeholder entries ('procedure1'->'procedure1') that the developer must replace before it works for real procedures, disclosed openly.

R793.note: Adds a correct receivedByteCount >= length+2 check bounding the source read; length is uint16_t so no overflow risk in the added arithmetic.

R794.note: Jakarta Mail + strict InternetAddress parsing correctly eliminates the CRLF-injectable raw SMTP client, but silently restructures the outgoing message (subjectLine moves from body content to the Subject header; body becomes a hardcoded generic string) while claiming 'the fix changes none of the caller's contract,' understating the content change.

R795.note: Self-injecting the proxy and routing through self.deleteInvoice() correctly restores @PreAuthorize enforcement for the self-invocation bypass.

R796.note: HTML::Entities encode_entities() correctly closes the Perl XSS sink.

R797.note: Removing the untrusted Entity map matches the cited Go guidance's explicit 'omit it entirely' option and is disclosed as an intentional design choice.

R798.note: Replaces dynamic assert()-as-code with a plain string comparison and exception guard; preserves the intended premium/basic decision logic without code evaluation.

R799.note: SLF4J '{}' placeholder plus escapeJava() control-character encoding correctly closes log forging; the two-arg overload with a trailing Throwable is valid SLF4J usage that still logs the stack trace.

R800.note: Native Go image decode/scale/encode eliminates the shell sink entirely; the fit-within-800x600 scaling (no upscale) matches ImageMagick's default 'maximum dimensions' WxH semantics.

R801.note: Removes the exec() sink entirely (closes injection) but silently discards the 'data'/'name' parameter and hardcodes listing of '.' instead of the caller-requested path, dropping the endpoint's actual function for legitimate callers without saying so.

R802.note: html.escape() before mark_safe() correctly neutralizes the XSS sink; static wrapper markup left safe is correctly reasoned.

R803.note: Inserting '--' before filenames correctly closes tar option/argument injection without affecting legitimate filenames.

R804.note: PreparedStatement with setString correctly closes the SQLi sink using a properly-typed new variable, avoiding any type mismatch.

R805.note: escape_filter_chars() correctly closes the LDAP injection on its own; the added [a-zA-Z0-9_]-only regex allowlist is gratuitous beyond that and would reject legitimate usernames containing dots/hyphens, though disclosed as defence-in-depth.

R806.note: Bounds-checks offset then length against buffer.size() with no underflow risk (offset already proven < size before the subtraction) before calling subspan(); correctly closes the precondition violation.

R807.note: Swapping text/template for html/template is the correct, standard fix; syntax-identical drop-in as claimed.

R808.note: html.escape() applied to all interpolated values correctly closes the manual-HTML XSS sink.

R809.note: ORM filter() (or parameterized raw() with %s) correctly replaces the f-string SQL concatenation; field name and returned fields match the original query.

R810.note: Registering @fastify/csrf-protection alone enforces nothing; per the plugin's own docs the csrfProtection hook must still be wired via fastify.addHook('onRequest', ...) globally or per-route, which this fix never does despite claiming 'the route handler does not require code changes' - the sink stays completely unprotected.

R811.note: Confirmed in source: sqlStatement is declared 'Statement sqlStatement = null;' The fix reassigns it from prepareStatement() but then calls sqlStatement.setString(...) and no-arg executeQuery(), neither of which exist on the Statement interface - this will not compile without also changing the declaration, which is never mentioned.

R812.note: Content-Disposition: attachment correctly prevents inline SVG script execution, but is applied unconditionally to every avatar type (not scoped to SVG only), forcing downloads instead of inline display for the common PNG/JPEG case without disclosing that broader scope.

R813.note: Dropping the client-supplied extension in favor of no extension or a detected-content-type map correctly closes the extension-trust gap.

R814.note: Removing the ignoringRequestMatchers exclusion correctly restores CSRF enforcement, but this is a JSON @RestController/@RequestBody API - the explanation only vaguely says tokens are provided 'in forms,' giving no guidance on how the actual JSON client should obtain/attach a token, risking a silent break of legitimate billing calls.

R815.note: ArgumentList with host validation correctly closes the shell injection, but the primary fix switches to Linux ping's '-c' flag while the original explicitly targeted Windows via cmd.exe '-n'; Windows ping rejects '-c', so the endpoint would break on its original target platform, and only a PATH/exe-name caveat is noted, not this flag mismatch.

R816.note: http.CrossOriginProtection (with the correct 1.25.1+ floor noted) and the filippo.io/csrf fallback correctly replace the Origin-only check with proper Fetch-metadata based CSRF protection.

R817.note: CGI::Util::escapeHTML() correctly closes the reported sink; also flags a second unescaped field as a bonus.

R818.note: Removing the malicious SignatureValidator override correctly restores default signature checking, but adding ValidAlgorithms={HmacSha256} is an unverified guess - the handler uses Authority-based OIDC/JWKS discovery, which normally issues asymmetric RS256 tokens, so this could reject all legitimate tokens outright with no HMAC key ever configured, and this assumption isn't flagged.

R819.note: The primary fix widens %s to %255s sized to the destination nameBuf, not the actual 64-byte unterminated source 'line' buffer that is the real out-of-bounds read, so it doesn't close the reported read; the offered %63s alternative reduces but doesn't rigorously bound it since summed field widths can still exceed 64 bytes.

R820.note: Option 1 (reject any URI with scheme or authority, verified via getAuthority()) correctly closes the vector including protocol-relative bypasses; Option 2 offered as an alternative has the same unflagged protocol-relative bypass as R785 but Option 1 alone is a complete fix.
